body.en: Calculus rests on a single idea: what value does a function approach as its input creeps toward a target? It need not ever reach that value — what matters is the trend.
We write \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \) if the outputs \( f(x) \) can be made as close to \( L \) as we like by taking \( x \) sufficiently close to \( c \) (but not equal to \( c \)).

The function may even be undefined exactly at \( c \). Consider \( \displaystyle f(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{x-1} \). At \( x=1 \) the formula gives \( \tfrac{0}{0} \), yet factoring reveals \( f(x)=x+1 \) everywhere else, so the curve heads straight for \( 2 \).

caption.en: Sampled points approaching the hole at x = 1

note.en: Slide from either side: \(f(x)\) marches to \(2\), even though the point at \(x=1\) is a hole.

body.en:
Sometimes the approach differs by direction. The left-hand limit \( \displaystyle \lim_{x\to c^-} f(x) \) and right-hand limit \( \displaystyle \lim_{x\to c^+} f(x) \) must agree for the two-sided limit to exist:

\[ \lim_{x\to c} f(x)=L \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lim_{x\to c^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to c^+}f(x)=L. \]

A function \( f \) is continuous at \( c \) when all three hold: (i) \( f(c) \) is defined, (ii) \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to c} f(x) \) exists, and (iii) the two are equal, \( \displaystyle\lim_{x\to c} f(x)=f(c) \). Informally: you can draw it through \( c \) without lifting the pen.

Evaluate \( \displaystyle \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{x^2-9}{x-3} \).

Direct substitution gives \( \tfrac00 \), so factor the numerator: \( x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3) \). Cancel the common factor (valid since \( x\neq 3 \) in the limit):

\[ \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3}=\lim_{x\to 3}(x+3)=6. \]

caption.en: Plot of rational function \(f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3}\) showing a removable discontinuity (hole) at \((3, 6)\).

body.en:
Indeterminate Form 0/0: Obtaining \(\frac{0}{0}\) from direct substitution does NOT mean the limit is 0, 1, or does not exist. It is an indeterminate form signaling that an algebraic simplification (factoring, conjugate rationalization, trig identity, or L'Hôpital's Rule) must be performed.

Two-Sided Limit Existence: The overall limit \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L\) exists IF AND ONLY IF both one-sided limits exist and agree: \(\lim_{x\to c^-} f(x) = \lim_{x\to c^+} f(x) = L\). For piece-wise and absolute value functions, always verify both directions separately.

Continuity Checklist: A function \(f\) is continuous at \(x = c\) only if all 3 conditions hold: (1) \(f(c)\) is defined; (2) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x)\) exists; (3) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = f(c)\).

solution.en: When \(x\) approaches 2 from the left (\(x < 2\)), \(x - 2 < 0\), so \(|x - 2| = -(x - 2)\). Substituting gives \(\lim_{x\to 2^-} \frac{-(x - 2)}{x - 2} = \lim_{x\to 2^-} (-1) = -1\). (Note: from the right, the limit is \(+1\), so the two-sided limit does not exist).
